name: @argszero/cordis-plugin-empty-response-retry
description: Makes an unattributed model attempt retryable, for the one seam that can tell. Three reports, one missing evidence. Discussion #8321: a `dsh-llm-pi-ai` route that relays an upstream empty response ends the turn, because `classifyPiAiError` has no rule matching the wording, so the text falls to the catch-all `PI_AI_ERROR`, and that is the one code `DEFAULT_RETRYABLE_CODES` does not carry (`EMPTY_RESPONSE`, `RATE_LIMIT`, `SERVER`, `TIMEOUT`, `TRANSPORT`) — `dsh-llm-retry` short-circuits on `!policy.retryableCodes.includes(failure.code)` and the step is never repeated, though the same adapter maps a locally detected zero-content completion to the retryable `EMPTY_RESPONSE`, so two paths that both mean "the model produced nothing" disagree. This plugin observes the public `llm/stream` waterfall — the one seam that sees an attempt and everything it produced — and rewrites that finish's `failure.code` to the by-value `EMPTY_RESPONSE` when the attempt ended in an unnamed error AND produced nothing at all; the retry executor then accepts the step on its own unchanged code gate. It is strictly narrower than the `retryableCodes: [..., PI_AI_ERROR]` workaround in the report, which widens every catch-all failure on a route: the two producers the adapter marks deliberately non-retryable (`pending`, `deferred` — a not-yet answer is not the safe repeat the principle is about) are excluded, as is any attempt that emitted a block, a token, or a Tool call, and any failure the adapter did name. Nothing buffered, nothing reordered, one boolean of state. 0.2.0 covers the same missing evidence from the other side of the classifier (discussion #9352): a gateway answered 400 with an EMPTY body, the HTTP client surfaced its own sentence for that (400 status code (no body) — the Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs share APIError.makeMessage), and classifyPiAiError's rule for the number matched the status inside the client's own sentence, so the turn was reported as INVALID_REQUEST — a name for the one word the client managed to write, not for anything that happened. That code is in no retryable table and no recovery path watches it (compaction keys on CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED alone), so every later turn re-sent the same transcript and failed at step 1: a twelve-minute provider blip bricked the session. The plugin now widens a second recognition, `statusOnlyCodes` (default INVALID_REQUEST), gated on the message by `statusOnlyMessages` being nothing but the client's own bodyless status line — a 400 that carries the provider's words is a diagnosis and is left exactly as it is. 0.3.0 acts on the finding behind the third report (discussion #9397), where a gateway's upstream-retry buffer limit (exceeded request buffer limit while retrying upstream — a 507 with no status number) fell to the catch-all and ended the turn. The observation generalizes: pi-ai decides retryability from a table of its own (RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN — 49 alternatives at 0.87.1, 55 at 1.1.0, measured by test/packaging.spec.mjs against the installed package), and the adapter's classifyPiAiError is a second, partial transcription of it — 24 of the reporter's 49 alternatives are wordings the chain cannot place. So a third recognition reads the same table on the way out: a failure whose code is in `transientCodes` and whose message matches `transientMessages` (the server-shaped half of pi-ai's own table) is rewritten to `transientTargetCode` (default SERVER, the name the chain would have written had it seen the digits), after `vetoMessages` declines pi-ai's NON_RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_LIMIT_ERROR_PATTERN first, exactly as pi-ai itself does. Unlike the first two recognitions it needs no produced-nothing condition, because the code is about the route, not about output — dsh-llm-retry gates on retryableCodes.includes(code) alone.
